Definition: a widow; also a desolate place
BiblicalUsage: The widow — and the Bible never lets her out of its sight. He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment. Learn to do well, Isaiah says; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow. God is a father of the fatherless and a judge of the widows in His holy habitation; and Zechariah's charge is plain: oppress not the widow, nor the fatherless, the stranger, nor the poor.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the widow is the test of whether a people knows God, because she has nothing to give back. The law, the prophets, the psalms and the restoration all say the same thing: the widow's cause is God's cause, and a religion that passes her by is not the religion of the Bible. I hold that how we treat the woman with no husband and no income tells the truth about us that our songs cannot hide.
